title: Understanding the Problem
text: To find the work required to stop the cylinder, we need to consider both its translational and rotational kinetic energy.

title: Translational Kinetic Energy
text: The translational kinetic energy of the cylinder is given by the formula: $$KE_{trans}$$ $$=$$ (1/2)*m*$$v**{2}$$, where $$m$$ is the mass and $$v$$ is the velocity.

title: Rotational Kinetic Energy
text: The rotational kinetic energy of the cylinder is given by the formula: $$KE_{rot}$$ $$=$$ (1/2)*I*$$\text{omega}**{2}$$, where I is the moment of inertia and omega is the angular velocity.

title: Moment of Inertia for a Cylinder
text: The moment of inertia for a solid cylinder is $$I=(1/2)mr**{2}$$.

title: Relating Linear and Angular Velocity
text: The angular velocity omega can be related to the linear velocity v by the formula: $$\omega=\frac{v}{r}$$.

title: Calculate Translational Kinetic Energy
text: Using the formula $$KE_{trans}$$ $$=$$ (1/2)*m*$$v**{2}$$, calculate the translational kinetic energy of the cylinder.
